title: Shinnecock Veterans and Wartime Service
summary: Shinnecock military service spans multiple American wars and remains part of community remembrance, family history, and public memorial traditions.
content:
Lois Marie Hunter devoted a chapter of her 1950 book to Shinnecock wartime service. Her account places military participation within a longer history of Native citizenship, community responsibility, and remembrance. The names and conflicts below are presented as Hunter recorded them; individual units, dates, and duties require military-record and Shinnecock Nation verification.

Service across generations

Hunter wrote that Shinnecock people participated in the Revolutionary War, Civil War, and World War I. For World War I she named Archibald Williams, William McKinley Cuffee, Lawrence Cuffee, Benjamin Harrison Hunter, and Paul Cuffee Eleazer, while noting that others were enrolled when the armistice was signed.1

World War II and the Korean conflict

Hunter identified George Kellis Davis as a Shinnecock member of an early Southampton Town contingent entering training under the Selective Service system. She printed a longer community honor roll for World War II and acknowledged that her list was incomplete because some Shinnecock service members were away from the reservation when names were gathered. At the time of publication, she also named Richard Smith, Arthur Ashman, Walter Wise Jr., and Norman Smith in connection with the Korean conflict.

Remembering service

The value of Hunter's chapter is not only its list of names. It records how military service was remembered within Shinnecock community history and provides a starting point for future service-record research. The Shinnecock Indian Reservation timeline also records the veterans' memorial plaque dedicated in 1981.

World War I and the Armistice

Hunter named Archibald Williams, William McKinley Cuffee, Lawrence Cuffee, Benjamin Harrison Hunter, and Paul Cuffee Eleazer as Shinnecock volunteers in World War I. She added that other Shinnecock men were enrolled when the Armistice was signed on November 11, 1918. The names are retained as Hunter’s community record while individual units, enlistment dates, and duties await service-record confirmation.1

World War II mobilization

Hunter identified George Kellis Davis among an early Southampton Town contingent entering training under the new Selective Service system. She described additional volunteers and draftees and printed an honor roll that she acknowledged was incomplete. This account shows how federal mobilization reached Shinnecock families, but it does not establish an exact induction date or complete service file for each person.2

References

  • Lois Marie Hunter, The Shinnecock Indians (Buys Bros., 1950), PDF pp. 43–44 (book pp. 84–86).
activity_update_summary: Added Hunter’s dated World War I Armistice account and World War II Selective Service context while keeping individual service details source-qualified.
